text:
emily (eng-infra): noticing spike in NAT failures from edge pods in us-west-2, model pulls timing out and retries spiking. logs show lots of 504 from nat-gw and high TIME_WAIT on nodes.
omar (eng-edge): yup seeing same from gpu-pool-a. thousands of TIME_WAIT, approx ~38k per node. model downloads stall then OOM on some allocator loops.
vikram (eng-platform): quick check — are they hitting S3 or external model registry?
emily (eng-infra): mostly S3 (model shards) + some external registries for containers. pattern: fanout of short-lived connections during scale-up.
zoe (ml infra): that explains the GPU boot failures — container can't fetch weights fast enough so kube liveness restarts. can we throttle parallel pulls?
omar (eng-edge): rolled a temporary rate limit on model-puller sidecar (concurrency 8 -> 2) for a subset of nodes, reduced immediate pressure.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0320-01 - NAT ephemeral exhaustion detected in us-west-2. Severity: high.
emily (eng-infra): diagnostic snippets:
```
# on node
$ netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l
38012
$ sysctl net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range
net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range = 32768	60999
$ curl -v https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/model-bucket/shard -i
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com (52.xx.xx.xx) port 443 (#0)
* Expire in 0 ms for 6 (transfer 0x55f...)
* Failed to receive HTTP/2 SYN_STREAM
* Connection timed out
```
omar (eng-edge): current ephemeral range leaves ~28k ports. with a lot of short-lived connections and NAT mapping overhead, we hit SNAT mapping exhaustion.
vikram (eng-platform): immediate mitigations we can try (short list):
- add S3 VPC endpoint in the affected subnets (removes NAT for S3 traffic)
- provision additional NAT GW elastic IPs / gateways across AZs
- enable long-lived connection pooling in sidecar (keepalive reuse)
- throttle model pull concurrency during scale-up
- sysctl tweaks: expand ip_local_port_range and tcp_tw_reuse (but careful)
emily (eng-infra): I've opened a PR to increase sidecar keepalive + connection pooling and toggled concurrency for the rollout group.
zoe (ml infra): can we get an S3 VPC endpoint quick? that'll stop a large majority of egress for model pulls.
vikram (eng-platform): provisioning VPC endpoint now, should be up in ~5-10m for the affected VPC. also spinning up a temporary NAT gateway in the 3rd AZ to distribute mappings.
deploy-bot: deploy started for sidecar v2.3.1 -> v2.3.2 (keepalive + connection re-use).
omar (eng-edge): after throttling + sidecar deploy, node TIME_WAIT dropped to ~6k within a minute on one test instance. requests recovered.
emily (eng-infra): added these tactical items to runbook:
- prefer VPC endpoints for S3 and ECR
- apply connection pooling in model-puller sidecar by default
- on fast scale-ups, gate parallel pulls with token bucket (default 10/min per node)
- monitor per-nat-gw ephemeral map usage (CloudWatch custom metric)
- fallback: add more nat-gw / elastic IPs per AZ
zoe (ml infra): longer-term: consider a blob cache on local SSDs on GPUs and pre-warm during scale decisions. reduces fanout at bootstrap.
vikram (eng-platform): agree. also tracking a change to encourage larger multipart pulls (fewer connections) and to centralize heavy external downloads through a dedicated egress proxy with multiplexing.
emily (eng-infra): incident status: mitigated, model pulls restored to normal for affected pools. continuing to monitor. tagging owners for follow-ups and a short blameless postmortem.
sre-bot: INC-2026-0320-01 status -> mitigated. follow-up tasks created in backlog. :white_check_mark:
omar (eng-edge): logs/alerts still noisy but trending down. will keep the throttles for 2 hours then re-evaluate.
zoe (ml infra): thanks all — saved a few GPUs from boot storms.
emily (eng-infra): filing action items: 1) VPC endpoints for S3 + ECR in prod us-west-2, 2) sidecar pool rollout, 3) runbook updates + dashboard (per-nat ephemeral usage). assigning owners.
vikram (eng-platform): I'll own the dashboard + metric. emily/omar/zoe please coordinate the component changes.
emily (eng-infra): thanks team. closing thread after postmortem write-up.
